concept: Timeline-from-witnesses — solver must interview witnesses for scattered "immediately before/after" adjacency clues about 5 murder-night events, chain them into a full order via elimination (no direct feedback on *which* position is wrong), then submit under a 10-step budget.
Alternating-regime population sequence — solver must locate the hidden switch point between additive and multiplicative growth to extrapolate an unseen future value.

Farm Plot Assignment — a 3×3 hidden-yield matching problem where the solver must scout plot–crop yield pairs under a step budget too small to reveal all nine, then commit a one-shot bijective assignment (each crop used exactly once) to maximize total yield.

Counterfeit gem identification — a ternary-outcome balance-scale search over 15 gems where the solver must track eliminated suspects itself across turns, since the scale reports only LEFT_HEAVIER/RIGHT_HEAVIER/BALANCED and never a running count.

Mosaic Border Drift — a repeating tile motif that shifts forward through a fixed color cycle each time it repeats; the solver must infer the hidden period and shift from partial evidence to predict specific hidden tiles.

Bracket Max-Min Seeding — the solver must prove (not guess) the overall strongest and weakest of four teams via pairwise strength queries, then submit the semifinal pairing that analytically minimizes the whole bracket's expected-upset probability, with all rewards computed from a hidden numeric strength model.

Banquet Seating Deduction — a round table of 6 guests where every probe returns only a coarse ADJACENT/OPPOSITE/APART verdict, forcing the solver to reconstruct the full clockwise cycle (up to the table's mirror symmetry) by elimination under a tight query budget.

CA Rule Detective — the solver must query a hidden, left-right-symmetric elementary cellular automaton's local update rule (8 neighborhoods, only 6 independent) through targeted probes, then hand-simulate forward from a given generation-0 row to predict three specific cells several generations later, using only the light cone of cells that actually matters.

Green Wave Signal Offset Search — solver must localize each intersection's hidden green window via ternary bisection feedback (TOO_EARLY/TOO_LATE/HIT) and allocate a shared 10-step probe budget across three signals tightly enough that a perfectly efficient search just barely fits before the final commit.

Median-Weight Gem — among 7 gems solver must use binary (never-balanced) weighings to build a transitive order and prove which single gem has exactly three others lighter and three heavier, rewarding both the proof milestone and the final correct identification.

Rotating-Key Substitution Cipher — the solver must infer a hidden per-position shift progression from a handful of costly oracle probes (fewer than the message length), then extrapolate the untested positions and invert the cipher to recover a hidden word, without ever being told the rule is linear.

Hidden-Calorie Hike Pack — a 0/1 knapsack where item weights are known upfront but calories are hidden behind ranges until spent inspection steps reveal them, forcing the solver to budget information-gathering against a hard step limit before committing one irreversible subset.

Unknown-Direction Fake Gem — among 8 identical-looking gems, exactly one is fake and either heavier or lighter (direction unknown) than the rest; the solver must use three-outcome balance weighings (LEFT_HEAVIER/RIGHT_HEAVIER/BALANCED) to narrow a 16-hypothesis space (8 gems × 2 directions) and commit to one irreversible final guess.

Fill-In Groove — the solver reads three notated bars of a drum pattern whose hit-count rises by a fixed hidden step each bar and whose hits within any bar are always spread by one fixed (undisclosed) evenness rule, then must extrapolate two bars ahead to reconstruct Bar 5 exactly, using a tightly budgeted set of single-position oracle probes to nail the rule's exact tie-breaking rather than brute-forcing all 16 steps.

Economic Dispatch Under Hidden Cost Curves — solver must probe rising marginal-cost functions and hidden capacities across three energy sources, then commit a continuous MW allocation that meets an exact demand target while minimizing total generation cost via the equal-marginal-cost principle, under a tight combined probe-and-commit step budget.

Two-Flip Parity Vault — 8 face-down cards, exactly two secretly flipped, and every probe returns only a coarse ODD/EVEN parity of how many flipped cards lie in a chosen subset, forcing the solver to triangulate both hidden positions via linear elimination rather than direct reveals, under a 10-step budget with verifiable candidate-narrowing milestones.

Mystery Base Numeral Cracker — solver must bisect a hidden base (6–16) using numeral-length transitions, then query the meanings of only the specific letters appearing in a 2-digit challenge numeral, and finally combine base and per-symbol values positionally to recover the challenge's decimal value.

Hidden-Capacity Expedition Sled — items and their weights/values are fully known, but the sled's true weight capacity is a hidden integer in a stated range; the solver must probe candidate loads for FITS/TOO HEAVY verdicts to narrow the capacity before a single irreversible commit maximizes packed value.

Blocked-Aisle Shelf Placement — one of four aisles is secretly slowed by a stray delivery cart, and a hard 2-probe budget can't always pin down which one, forcing the solver to hedge a frequency-weighted item-to-slot assignment under genuine residual uncertainty.

Blight-Adjusted Harvest Split — allocate 10 whole acres across wheat/corn/soy with known diminishing-returns yield tables for two crops, but corn's yield is scaled by a hidden blight severity (one of five levels) that must be probed via two small test plots before an irreversible whole-farm commit.

Round-Robin Standings Deduction — 5 teams played a full round robin under a hidden strict strength order (no draws); the solver spends a tight, sub-sorting-theoretic query budget on pairwise results, then commits a full final standings order, with genuine residual ambiguity built in because the budget is deliberately short of what's needed to fully resolve all 120 possible orderings.

Digit-Root Vending Machine — a hidden multiplier K (2–8) transforms any fed token's value, revealing only the transformed digital root; two of three catalog tokens are digital-root-multiples-of-3 and so can only ever pin K down to one of 2–3 candidates sharing a residue mod 3 (never more, by number-theoretic necessity), while the third token is a digital-root-multiple-of-9 trap that leaks nothing at all — forcing a genuine residual guess among distinct outcomes when predicting an untested coprime challenge token.

Tainted Mint Batch — a cashier's coin drawer has one of three higher-value denominations secretly recalled as counterfeit; a single audit narrows suspicion but (in the realistic worst case) still leaves a coin-flip between two candidates, forcing the solver to balance exploiting high-value coins for fewer-coin change against the risk of an irreversible refused payment.

Night Bridge Plank Check — a rope bridge has one secretly rotten plank among 8; a torch with only two uses gives coarse CREAK/SOLID group-test verdicts before an irreversible crossing commit, forcing the solver to binary-search down to 2 residual suspects and then guess.

Mystery Planet Conjunction Tracker — solver must identify a hidden orbital period from six close-spaced candidates using only coarse angular-separation buckets returned at chosen probe days, then extrapolate the discovered periodic pattern to predict a future conjunction date under tolerance-banded scoring.

Green-Wave Offset Tuner — the platoon's true cruising speed is a single hidden unknown (5 discrete candidates); a hard 2-of-3 probe budget with coarse (nearest-5-second) timing readouts leaves genuine multi-way ambiguity, forcing the solver to set three downstream signal offsets that hedge across the surviving speed candidates rather than compute a closed-form green wave.
